segments: Yovel 11.
Arab Kings.
a wooden cross
weighing four Baghdad litras,
should be killed.
And also, a Jew who did not hang from his neck a block of wood
in the shape of a bell-clapper {OCR?}
weighing six litras {OCR: ܓܝܼܛܪܹ̈ܐ for ܠܝܼܛܪܹ̈ܐ},
should be killed.
And when they entered the baths, they were to tie small bells to their necks,
so that they might be distinguished from the Arabs.
This persecution began from a certain Christian-hater,
who reported to al-Hakim the caliph:
"When the Christians assemble to celebrate Easter in the temple in Jerusalem,
the keepers of the church scheme,
and with balsam oil they smear the iron wire by which the lamp above the Tomb is suspended.
And when the governor of the Arabs seals the door of the Tomb,
they light a fire from the roof at the top of the iron wire,
and the fire runs down to the wick and kindles it.
And thus they cry 'Kyrie eleison' and weep,
as though they see light descending from heaven upon the Tomb,
and they are confirmed in their faith."
And when the Christians and Jews had remained in such distress for some time,
before the time when al-Hakim the caliph was killed, he repented of his deed,
and ordered that those who had apostatized should return again to their faith.
And he permitted the Christians,
and they rebuilt their churches better than they had been previously.
And those who had fled to the territory of the Romans
returned again to their homes.
And in the year four hundred of the Arabs,
Abu Nasr Bashir bar Harun bar Kammala {OCR: Gamala}, the Christian scribe, died in Baghdad, on the 26th
of the month of Shawwal.
And in the year 401 {OCR: ܝܬܐ for ܬܩܐ or similar},
401 of the Arabs, Qirwash (Qarawush?) bar al-Muqallad, the ruler of Mosul,
proclaimed al-Hakim, the caliph of Egypt.
And much locust was seen in the region of Mosul,
and the 'Uqaylids {OCR: ܡܲܥܕܵܝܹ̈ܐ for ܥܘܼܩܲܝܠܵܝܹ̈ܐ/Ma'addites?} raided the land from every side,
and there was also a great pestilence.
And famine became severe in the region of Khorasan,
to the point that a litra of bread was sold for a gold dinar.
And human beings ate dogs and cats {OCR: ܟܟܘܫܝܬܐ for ܟܘܫܝܬܐ/ܟܛܘ̈ܬܐ},
and after that, infants and children.
And after that, they would leap upon whomever they saw who was fat and fleshy,
and they would kill him and eat [him].
And in the year 403,
403 of the Arabs,
the wife of Abu Nasr bar Isra'il, the Christian jurist (nomikos), died in Baghdad;
and they carried her bier in the daytime,
